advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor test_the_refusal_creates_no_clone_on_the_underlying_directory to producer liveness (assert res['status']=='deferred' and g.clone_calls==0) so its absence assertions cannot pass vacuously when the guard is never reached.
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:3464 `_run_review(g, tmp_path)` — return value discarded, so no res['status']/gap_reason liveness anchor
tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:3466-3468 assert g.seen_during_clone == []; assert list(...glob('reviewbot-*')) == []; assert sorted(...iterdir()) == [] — three absence-only assertions

tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:3415-3417 `seen_during_clone` is appended ONLY inside `clone_change_ref`, which is not invoked on the refusal path, making that assertion trivially [] regardless of behaviour

The liveness anchor (`assert g.clone_calls == 0`) lives in a different test (test_unmounted_scratch_refuses_the_review_bot_clone, line 3446), not in this AC3 test, so this absence oracle is unanchored on its own terms (fail-open oracle: definite-pass world includes 'the review never reached the guard').
advisory.finding: The AC3 absence test asserts nothing about producer liveness: it discards the review result (no res['status'] check) and never asserts clone_calls == 0, while g.seen_during_clone is only populated inside clone_change_ref (never called on the refusal path). All three absence assertions therefore pass vacuously if the review path short-circuits before the pre-clone scratch guard for any reason, so the test cannot distinguish 'guard refused correctly' from 'the guard was never reached'.
scenarios: A future change moves or removes the pre-clone scratch guard, or a preceding voter guard begins short-circuiting before it; the review yields no clone but for the wrong reason and the AC3 test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_the_refusal_creates_no_clone_on_the_underlying_directory, capture the result (`res, _ = _run_review(g, tmp_path)`) and add `assert res['status'] == 'deferred'` and `assert g.clone_calls == 0` before the absence assertions.
